analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182 picks a random extra delay of 0, 1 or 2 independently for each bit. With a coherent synchronized pointer, occ <= 8 and o_full_thr(thr=8) is identical to o_full. analyses.spec_says: contract.json:365: "(a) At every rising edge of i_clk_wr with i_rst_n_wr=1: N <= PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH (8), and if N == PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_full=1. (b) At every rising edge of i_clk_rd ... if N == 0 and P is empty, then o_empty=1." spec.md:137-138 REQ-FUNC-008/009.
analyses.rtl_does: No RTL defect is indicated for the bulk of the failures. They occur with the plain chain (CHK-006 fails=8910 in syn.s1.log:21792 and model_off.s1.log:21803), while the Python CHK-006 checks (py:217-220 and py:264-266) pass in those runs (e.g. model_off test 014 passed, model_off.s1.log:637, while SVA CHK-006 failed at @435000, model_off.s1.log:63).
analyses.test_does: nnc_chk_sb.sv:109-119 uses q_n and p_n from the same reference-model block (lines 55-99). That block misses clock edges because of its edge detection (lines 55-59: posedge-only sensitivity with m_rd_clk_q/m_wr_clk_q updated only when the block wakes). Missed read edges mean no pops, so q_n grows past the real occupancy. That gives 'q_n==8 but o_full=0' or 'q_n>8' (a_CHK_006, line 109-112), firing every 14 ns (the write period) in model_off.s1.log:63-76. Missed write edges similarly break a_CHK_006_rd.

candidates.evidence_for: It shares the reference model with CHK-005, so the same edge-detection bug applies (nnc_chk_sb.sv:55-59). It fails in all configurations, the Python model with the same definition passes, and the failure cadence follows the clock periods.
candidates.evidence_against: In model-on runs some genuine optimistic-flag events can occur (see CHK-003/013), but the broken reference model hides them.

analyses.failure: Assertion CHK-011 — o_sw_rst_busy falls only after i_rst_n_sw=1 plus a round trip (1 fail @73245000, base.s2 only)
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:492: "Suppose o_sw_rst_busy=1 at write edge m and 0 at write edge m+1, with i_rst_n_wr=1 throughout. Then (a) ... k <= m-(S+1) ...". It does not mention i_rst_n_rd. contract.json:757-758 CHK-023 Part 3: "assert only i_rst_n_rd in the middle of it ... The handshake after a one-domain reset is not checked." rules.json:4268: "If only one domain gets a hardware reset during a software reset, the handshake can wait forever for the other domain; the IP does not repair it (ASM-005 applies)." rules.json:10729 DEC-031: "A hardware reset of one domain only during the sequence is not repaired."
analyses.rtl_does: The failure falls inside test_chk_023 (71560.40-73693.40 ns, base.s2.log:6763-6767). Part 3 (py:1202-1223) resets only the read domain while the write FSM is in REQ/HOLD with i_rst_n_sw=0. The read reset clears reg_ack_rd and reg_rgray (rd.sv:141-146, 189-194). Right after the read release, the test drives i_rst_n_sw=1 (py:1220). The write FSM goes HOLD->REL (wr.sv:180-183). REL->RUN only needs !w_ack_s && w_rgray_s=='0 (wr.sv:184-187), and both already hold because the read domain was just reset and has not re-acknowledged. So busy falls one edge after the edge sampling i_rst_n_sw=1, which breaks (a) k <= m-3. This is the 'not repaired' one-domain-reset behaviour the spec accepts.
analyses.test_does: nnc_chk_wr.sv:98-101: (o_sw_rst_busy) |=> (busy || ($past(busy_ok) && ...)), disable iff (!i_rst_n_wr) only. busy_ok needs 2 edges after i_rst_n_sw=1 is seen while busy (lines 50-63). It is not disabled or re-armed after an i_rst_n_rd assertion. Stimulus py:1211-1221 deliberately does a read-only reset mid-sequence (contract CHK-023 Part 3).

candidates.evidence_for: The single failure is in the CHK-023 Part 3 window. The contract says the handshake after a one-domain reset is not checked (contract.json:758), and the spec says the IP does not repair this case (rules.json:4268, 10729; ASM-005). The SVA does not exclude busy intervals during which i_rst_n_rd was asserted. CHK-011 has 0 fails in all other 13 runs, including about 1500 hits with many software resets (syn.s1.log:21788).
candidates.evidence_against: Without a waveform the exact time cannot be tied to Part 3 with certainty; it is inferred from the test window and the mechanism.

candidates.evidence_for: CHK-011's wording (contract.json:492) requires only i_rst_n_wr=1 throughout, not i_rst_n_rd, so read literally it also applies after a read-only reset. That conflicts with CHK-023's 'not checked' and DEC-031.
candidates.evidence_against: The higher-level spec decisions (DEC-031, ASM-005) are explicit that this case is out of scope.

candidates.evidence_for: The early busy fall leaves the read FSM possibly re-entering RST/ACK after the write side is in RUN.
candidates.evidence_against: The spec accepts this outcome explicitly (rules.json:4268, 10729), and the RTL REL exit condition (wr.sv:184-187) is the documented flush check.

analyses.rtl_does: wr.sv:102 w_wr_blk = reg_sw_rst_busy | ~i_rst_n_sw and wr.sv:125-126 o_full / o_full_thr depend combinationally on i_rst_n_sw. This zero-latency block is required by CHK-009 (contract.json:444). So when i_rst_n_sw falls, o_full rises and o_full_thr goes to (thr==0) in that same time step. o_overflow and o_sw_rst_busy are flops (wr.sv:158-163, 208-213, 224-225).
analyses.test_does: The Python driver changes i_rst_n_sw at FALLING edges of i_clk_wr (wstep, py:286-295, docstring 'Called at a write falling edge'; Traffic.writer py:415-417; test 023 py:1158, 1165, 1187, 1192, 1207, 1220). nnc_chk_wr.sv:65-70 snapshots {o_overflow, o_sw_rst_busy, o_full, o_full_thr} at negedge i_clk_wr. The snapshot runs before the cocotb write in that same falling-edge time step, so it holds the pre-request o_full. a_CHK_012 (lines 105-107) then finds a different o_full at the next posedge. The checker has no exemption for i_rst_n_sw changes. Failures line up one-to-one with software-reset requests: base.s2.log:6786, 6795, 6818 give 3 fails during test 023, which issues 3 requests. syn.s1.log:15110-15115 gives 5 fails during test 027, which pulses i_rst_n_sw 5 times (contract.json:894). The stimulus also drives i_rst_n_sw at falling edges, exactly when the snapshot is taken, instead of at rising edges as spec.md:556 describes. analyses.failure: Assertion CHK-013 — o_full_thr consistency (59 fails / 208870 hits, first at 1681000; 0 fails in model_off and syn)
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:524: "(c) if i_full_thr==PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_full_thr == (o_full AND i_rst_n_sw AND NOT o_sw_rst_busy); (d) if o_full=1, i_rst_n_sw=1 and o_sw_rst_busy=0, then o_full_thr == (i_full_thr <= PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH)." spec.md:139 REQ-FUNC-010 (estimate pessimistic for the full side); spec.md:137 REQ-FUNC-008; spec.md:181 REQ-VER-001 (independent per-bit model with replacement); spec.md:684-685 (model claimed to show only the previous pointer and keep flags pessimistic); spec.md:1246 TEST-008 ('flags never optimistic').
analyses.rtl_does: wr.sv:120 w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s; wr.sv:126 o_full_thr = (w_occ >= i_full_thr); wr.sv:106,125 o_full from a Gray equality. These agree for any coherent synchronized pointer (occ in 0..8). The model in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182 delays each bit independently by 0-2 extra cycles and replaces pending changes. Bits of w_rgray_s can therefore update out of order, giving a value ahead of the source read pointer (e.g. 0010=3 while the source is at 0011=2). Then w_occ wraps to 9..15, so o_full_thr=1 and o_full=0. Counts: 'CHK-013 ... fails=0' in syn.s1.log:21790 and model_off.s1.log:21801. The failures coincide with the Python monitor failures (sim.log:164 at 1680.69 ns and sim.log:249 @1681000; sim.log:6282/6328).
analyses.test_does: nnc_chk_wr.sv:111-117 codes (a)-(d) of contract.json:524 directly, disable iff (!i_rst_n_wr). It is an independent implementation of the same rule as py:196-204.

candidates.evidence_for: The failure appears only with the model enabled. The model behaviour is exactly what REQ-VER-001 (spec.md:181) and 10.6.4 (spec.md:653) prescribe. The spec's assumption that a late bit only shows 'the previous pointer value' (spec.md:684) and keeps flags pessimistic (spec.md:685, TEST-008) does not hold when two Gray updates arrive within the extra-delay window. The spec contradicts REQ-FUNC-008/010.
candidates.evidence_against: If the requester intended a coherent model, the spec wording is merely incomplete and the defect sits in the model RTL (A).

candidates.evidence_for: The incoherent pointer is created by rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182. Real synchronizers on Gray code cannot produce a value ahead of the source.

analyses.options: The designer decides on REQ-VER-001: (1) require a coherent model, i.e. a synchronized Gray vector never shows a value the source has not had. Possible ways: the extra delay only chooses old or new at the capture edge; or no bit's pending change can be overtaken by a later change of another bit; or the delay is applied per vector (this touches DEC-039). Then fix m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182 and correct spec.md:684-685. Or (2) keep the current model and state in the spec that it can create states that real hardware cannot, and decide which checks apply to model-on runs. That is a scope decision; CHK-013 itself should stay as written.
